This message comes from MattressFirm.
Restless partner keeping you up, MattressFirm sleep experts can match you with a Tempur-Pedic
that absorbs motion.
Save up to $1,000 on select Tempur-Pedic split-king sleep systems during the Black Friday sale.
They make sleep easy.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
China says it plans to retaliate if the U.S. moves ahead with proposed new tariffs.
The warning comes as the two countries negotiate a long-term trade agreement, as NPR's Jennifer
Pack reports.
The U.S. wants to impose new tariffs on the European Union and 13 countries, including
China.
U.S. tariffs on Chinese exports could go up to 20 percent or as high as 40 percent.
And the Trump administration says this is a response to excess capacity, something China's
foreign ministry rejects.
The so-called issue of overcapacity is a false proposition, says spokesperson Guo Jia-kun,
using it as a pretext for political manipulation, he says.
President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping have had three friendly meetings this year,
but the underlying U.S.-China relationship remains tense.
Jennifer Pack, NPR News, Beijing.
Thanksgiving Day weather brought power outages to hundreds of thousands of Americans, mostly
due to heavy rain, strong winds and coastal flooding on the East Coast.
But Missouri got socked with heavy snow.
Jackie Becker is with the Amaran Power Company.
This system involved very heavy, wet snow.
And so that combined with trees that still have leaves on, in many cases, has really
resulted in a significant amount of tree damage.
And that tree damage then, in turn, unfortunately has caused many outages on our lines.
According to the online tracker, poweroutage.us, Missouri homes and businesses account for
some 90,000 outages, a total more than 870,000, the bulk of the outages, stretch along the
East Coast from North Carolina to Connecticut and New York.
Strobe Talbot has died.
Talbot's son says his father passed away Thursday after a long illness at his home in East Hampton,
New York.
He's 30 years old.
Talbot was a former Time Magazine reporter and Deputy Secretary of State under President
Bill Clinton.
Lawmakers gearing up for a legislative sprint after the holiday, NPR's Barbara Sprunt reports
on a long to-do list when Congress returns from Thanksgiving.
High up on the agenda is funding the government.
Funding is set to expire on December 11th.
Congress has to either pass a dozen appropriations bills or approve another stopgap measure,
known as a continuing resolution.
Passing a CR would keep the government open and bypass another government shutdown.
The House will decide when to take up a permitting reform package as well, aimed at speeding
up the building of the nation's infrastructure.
The Senate has already passed the measure.
And there's also a leadership election in the Senate, where Democratic senators will
pick their next majority leader.
Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen is challenging New York Senator Chuck Schumer for the top
job.
This is Barbara Sprunt, NPR News, Washington.
And you're listening to NPR News.
French actor Gerard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually
assaulting a young actress at his home in Paris in 2018.
The Paris Court of Appeal made the ruling Thursday after rejecting his bid to avoid
having the case tried, Depardieu denies the allegations.
Major League Baseball approaching an expected lockout of players once the current labor
agreement between the owners and the players' union expires December 1st, and period Sean
Stolena says more.
Owners want to establish a salary cap and floor for players.
They say a cap would allow smaller market teams, like the world champion brewers, to
better compete with big spending teams like the Dodgers and Mets.
Major League Baseball Commissioner Rob Manfred says he believes most fans want this too.
They want a salary cap and floor, and on that we will not compromise.
But the players' union disagrees and is adamant that any new agreement cannot include a cap
on players' salaries.
As the two sides dig in, there are worries this lockout could extend into the regular
season in March.
The last time games were lost due to a labor dispute was following the players' strike
of 1994 and '95.
John Stolena, NPR News.
A bronze medal rower who is credited with giving women a voice in Olympic policymaking
has died.
LaNita de France was 74.
The International and U.S. Olympic Committees announced her death Thursday, no cause was
given.
De France was the first American woman and first black American named to the International
Olympic Committee in 1986.
She was also the first woman to serve as the IOC's vice president.
This is NPR News.
